title: Conduct a scheduled service on agricultural equipment

lessons.title: Why we service and how to plan it
lessons.html:
What is a scheduled service?

A scheduled service is maintenance done at set times. On a tractor the time is counted in engine hours on the hour meter, for example every 250 or 500 hours. The service book or operator manual says what to do at each service. Follow the manual for your machine, not your memory.

Good servicing:

  • stops breakdowns in the busy season, like planting or harvest;
  • makes the engine use less diesel;
  • makes the machine last longer;
  • saves money – a filter costs a few hundred rand, a new engine costs a lot more.

Planning the service

  1. Check the hour meter and the service record. Find which service is due.
  2. Read the service checklist in the manual for that service.
  3. Get the parts: filters, oil, grease, belts. Check the part numbers match the machine.
  4. Get the tools and a drip tray, rags and a used-oil drum.
  5. Book the machine with the farm manager so it is not needed in the field.

Work safely

  • Park on level ground, lower the implements to the ground, pull the handbrake and switch off. Take the key out.
  • Let the engine cool. Hot oil and a hot radiator can burn you badly. Never open a hot radiator cap.
  • Wear gloves, safety glasses and safety boots.
  • Keep fire away. Diesel and oil burn. No smoking in the workshop.
  • Clean up spills right away so nobody slips.

lessons.title: Doing the service checklist
lessons.html:
Typical service tasks

Every machine is different, but most services include these tasks. Tick each one off on the checklist as you finish it.

TaskWhat to do
Engine oil and filterDrain warm (not hot) oil, change filter, fill with the right grade to the full mark.
Fuel filtersChange filters, bleed air out of the fuel system as the manual shows.
Air filterClean or replace. Check the hose clamps and the dust bowl.
CoolantCheck level when cold. Check hoses for cracks.
BeltsCheck for cracks and correct tightness.
Grease pointsWipe each nipple clean and grease until fresh grease shows.
Transmission and hydraulic oilCheck level on the dipstick or sight glass.
BatteryClean terminals, check they are tight.
TyresCheck pressure and look for cuts.

Good habits

  • Wipe around a filler cap before you open it so dust does not get in.
  • Put a little clean oil on a new filter seal and tighten by hand as the filter says.
  • Use only the oil grade in the manual. The wrong oil can damage the gearbox or hydraulics.
  • Look for problems while you work: leaks, loose bolts, worn tyres, broken lights. Report them.

lessons.title: Checking, recording and handing over
lessons.html:
After the service

  1. Check that all drain plugs and filters are tight and all caps are back on.
  2. Count your tools. No spanner or rag must be left in the engine bay.
  3. Start the engine and let it run. Watch the oil pressure light go out.
  4. Look under the machine for leaks around filters and plugs.
  5. Switch off, wait a few minutes and check the oil level again. Top up if needed.

Recording the service

Write the service on the service record or job card. Include:

  • date and hour meter reading;
  • which service was done;
  • parts and oil used, with quantities;
  • problems you found and reported;
  • your name.

On many farms this record goes into the farm system so the manager knows when the next service is due. A good record also helps when you claim on a warranty.

Waste

Used oil, old filters and dirty rags must go into the right drums or bins. Never burn them or bury them. Used oil can poison soil and water.

Handing over

Tell your supervisor the machine is ready and tell them about any faults that still need fixing.

Key points

  • Service at the hours given in the manual for that machine.
  • Let the engine cool and switch off before you start.
  • Use the right filters and the right oil grade.
  • Check for leaks and oil level after the engine has run.
  • Record the date, hours, parts and faults on the service record.

quiz.question: On a tractor, how is the time between services usually counted?

options.text: In engine hours on the hour meter

quiz.question: Why should you never open a hot radiator cap?

options.text: Hot coolant can spray out and burn you

quiz.question: How do you grease a grease point correctly?

options.text: Put grease on top of the dirt
Only grease it once a year
Wipe the nipple clean and grease until fresh grease shows
Use engine oil instead of grease

quiz.question: When should you check the engine oil level again after the service?

options.text: After the engine has run and stood for a few minutes

quiz.question: What should you do with old oil filters and dirty rags?

options.text: Put them in the right drums or bins
Leave them in the engine bay

quiz.question: Any oil will do for the gearbox and hydraulics, as long as it is clean.
